chunk_map.heading: ## Save the rule if it earned itself

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked line 44 ("Ask Claude whether these rules are auto-loaded into each session.") specifically: per dispatch note this is a known false positive rejected by the maintainer — "these rules" refers deliberately to whatever is loaded in the context window (a concept, not a named antecedent file), so it resolves without a prior naming. Line 91's "the M2 task" resolves against Prework's "Surface one multi-file backlog task" (chunk 2, prior in file). "STRIDE" at chunk 8 line 95 resolves against its own appositive definition at chunk 7 line 91 ("STRIDE, the six-category threat walk"), one chunk earlier. "the second-pass read"/"a second read" (chunks 5, 6, 7) resolves via module include-order: the concept is taught in the linked `push-back-on-the-plan` exercise, which precedes these chunks in deck order.

The M1 callback at chunk 2 ("if Dex Horthy's ... is still on your list from Module 1, this is the module it pays off in") names the source module directly (Module 1) rather than pointing by position. No other file is referenced by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "the M2 task" (chunk 7, line 89) resolves to the backlog task surfaced in Prework (chunk 2) and carried through push-back-on-the-plan; both beats exist in this module's current exercise set. No dead beat references found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construct present in this file.
Every chunk, including the single-sentence chunk 1 (Big Idea, architecture-mandated title-card content per module-shape.md, not stray buffered prose), carries a self-standing claim.
Every header's content matches its promise (Prework surfaces prework, What You'll Learn lists LOs, Next transitions, Pre-reads lists optional reads).

No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction, no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlative, no abstraction-noun stack, no empty-leg verb triplet found in body. The one number+hedge ("about 10%" in Key Concepts, chunk 6) has no attached retraction clause and is maintainer-attested as M1's carried prior (line 111 of the source), so the sub-item does not fire — harm (a claim stated then undercut) is absent; this is a held prior stated once.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/maintainer vocabulary (compendium, firing, forcing function, beat, mood, surface-as-noun, Connections-as-proper-noun) found in body text. All body vocabulary (push-back, plan mode, task, rule file) is ordinary engineering register.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 7 "Next" (no-module:earn-the-trust branch): line 87: "**Pick one scoped task you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit: a real slice. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**" — a whole two-sentence lead bolded, not a <=5-word handle. Harm check: same shape and same rationale (check_pedagogy §34's mandated task-sizing anti-pattern line) as the Prework bolded callout at line 12, which the maintainer block explicitly accepts by name ("do not flatten it, and do not re-raise it as a fresh finding") — but that accept-note scopes only to Prework's instance, not this one, so the harm this rule guards against (bold monoculture / diluted emphasis) is plausibly absent here for the identical reason, yet unattested at this specific location. Reporting as a rule question rather than assuming the Prework note extends here.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either extend the check_pedagogy §34 maintainer accept-note to cover this line too, or confirm with the maintainer whether it's deliberately unattested.
